Q1: Caffeine has officially recognized hazards related to carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, or reproductive toxicity (CMR1) and oral toxicity (ORL1) under the Globally Harmonized System. Expanded scientific data also indicates potential environmental, endocrine disruption, inhalation, and dermal/eye hazards (Tier 2). However, data is currently insufficient to assess its organ and systemic hazards (OGN4).
Q2: Caffeine is included on the TEDX List of Potential Endocrine Disruptors, indicating scientific evidence suggests it may interfere with the endocrine system. This aligns with its Tier 2 rating for endocrine disruption hazards (EDC2).
Q3: Caffeine is exceptionally well-characterized, with 68,000 scientific references, a precise molecular formula (C8H10N4O2), and classification as a well-defined "Small Molecule." Although organ and systemic hazards are currently data deficient (Tier 4), the extensive body of research indicates a comprehensive understanding of its profile.
